Volume Spread Analysis (Tom Williams, Gavin Holmes) reads each bar by its spread (range vs the last 20 bars), close (high / mid / low of the bar) and volume (vs the last 20 bars), against the background. Every sign is weighted by its context (trend, background, location): e.g. no demand inside a strong uptrend is usually just a pause, in a downtrend it is significant. Run over 1269 desk names (plus a compact read of all 2802 RS-universe names for the charts): every setup in the scanners (VCP, SEPA, power play, HTF, flat base, Wyckoff springs when present) plus the tracked names, each over its own base / range window. Context only: VSA never creates, removes or re-scores a setup or a spring. Tap a ticker for its report card; tap "story" for the narrative.

📐 VSA Sequences Gavin Holmes / TradeGuider trade set-up sequences completing in the last 10 bars · grouped bullish / bearish, then bars ago · display only, not scored2930

Each sequence is three VSA bars in order (A → B → C) inside 20 bars, touching a 20-bar high (bearish) or low (bullish). It fires on bar C, using only bars up to C (no look-ahead). Trigger = a stop order 0.1% beyond bar C (Holmes p.12: do not act on the no-demand / no-supply bar itself, the next bar must confirm); invalidation = the sequence extreme. ARMED = waiting for the trigger (live 3 bars) · TRIGGERED = traded through · EXPIRED / INVALIDATED = gone. "bt" = the one-year no-look-ahead backtest verdict for that sequence (feeds/backtest/vsa_sequences/report.md): edge = avg R > 2 SE above 0 and beats the drift baseline, noise = indistinguishable from 0R, negative = loses. These are not fed into the VSA balance, Setup Master or the A+++ alert.

📖 Signs & method

SCSelling climax (strength)
SVStopping volume (strength)
BHBag holding (strength)
SOShakeout (strength)
TTest (strength)
TTest in a rising market (strength)
NSNo supply (strength)
EREffort to rise (strength)
ABAbsorption volume (strength)
BCBuying climax (weakness)
UTUpthrust (weakness)
PUPseudo-upthrust (weakness)
NDNo demand (weakness)
EMEnd of a rising market (weakness)
EFEffort to fall (weakness)
FTPossible failed test (supply present) (weakness)
SQSquat bar (high volume, narrow spread) (context)

Bar measures: spread = high−low ÷ average of the prior 20 bars (wide ≥ 1.25×, narrow ≤ 0.75×); close position 0 (low) – 1 (high); volume ÷ prior 20-bar average (ultra high ≥ 2×, high ≥ 1.3×, low ≤ 0.8×, ultra low ≤ 0.5×); up/down bar = close vs prior close. Key rules: selling climax = wide down bar to a new 20-bar low on ≥ 2× volume after a decline, closing off the lows (or next bar up); stopping volume = heavy down bar in a reaction closing in its upper half, any spread (meaning set by trend: bullish in an uptrend, only a pause in a downtrend); no supply / no demand = narrow down / up bar on volume below the prior two bars; test = dips under the prior low, closes in the top 40% on low volume; test in a rising market (Holmes) = narrow down bar closing on the low on very low volume inside the prior bar, in an uptrend; upthrust = new short-term high, wide spread, closes in the lower quarter; buying climax = wide up bar into new highs on ≥ 2× volume closing mid/low after a run; end of a rising market = narrow up bar on ≥ 2× volume at new highs. Context brain: every sign is read against the trend at the bar before it (50-day slope, price vs 50-day, 20- vs 50-day, swing highs/lows; a ±15% 20-bar move overrides), the background (a climactic strength / weakness sign in the prior 30 bars) and the location (near range support / resistance, new 20-bar highs / lows). The context matrix above gives each sign × context a weight, polarity and reason (Williams / Holmes page refs); significance = bar match × weight × location. One context modifier: no demand in a downtrend / weak background followed within 5 bars by an upthrust is raised ×1.6 (Holmes p.81). Multi-bar Holmes trade set-up sequences (see 📐 VSA Sequences) are listed for display only and never scored. Balance 0–100 = recency-weighted sum of context-weighted signs plus the up-vs-down-bar volume ratio (≥ 60 strength, ≤ 40 weakness). Thresholds are desk calibration (Williams/Holmes publish none); pseudo-upthrust and squat are marked unverified in the method file. Confirmation uses the next bar, so older signs carry one bar of hindsight; today's bar is "awaiting next bar".

Sources: Tom Williams, Master the Markets (TradeGuider) and That Was The Week; Gavin Holmes, Trading in the Shadow of the Smart Money (page refs in the matrix; rules paraphrased). Price data to 2026-10-09; setup windows from the scan of 2026-10-09.
